title: Why he quit playing and his move to Pensacola
summary: Music was an avocation; he brought a band to Florida Town, stayed in Pensacola, and rose from CWA work to district director of employment.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Why did you quit playing? Well, like I was about to say, music has been an avocation with me more than for steady fare. And I have been successful. Like I came here on, the boys had never been out on the road with Geordie. And Mr. Pace here in Pensacola wanted us to come over here and play at Florida Town. So the band came over here under the name of Harold Geordie. But when Dave Johnson, a lot of them saw the band, they said, well, that's Norman Brownlee's band from New Orleans. Well, the thing was, a lot of the boys didn't want to go out on the road for the first time with Geordie. They knew that when they were with me, that I got them and managed them well and looked after their welfare pretty well. And they didn't know just how they'd fare with Harold, because he hadn't taken a band out before. Not that he wasn't capable or not that he wasn't a good person. But the fellas just kind of, they just, they said if I'd go, they'd go. So we had nothing else to do, my brother, so we came over here. And now you can't drag me away. I've been here ever since then. I got a job as a rodman and chainman with the engineering gang in CWA. And from that I argued out with the administrator here about setting up a warehouse and setting up projects to house some of the materials and charge it out. And I got to be a warehouseman and bookkeeper. And from there I got into a line that I was definitely proficient in, and that was personnel. And when I got into that I finally got to be assignment officer, and I wound up as district director of employment in charge of sixteen counties, so I didn't do bad in this spot. And I say be a musician or a laborer or what not. If a fella just goes into a community and behaves himself, he'll get along all right. And I've done well in Pensacola, and I guess I'm president of the union here. Did you want to hear anything like that? You didn't want my life's history, did you?
